description:
We are a team of ambitious high school students united by our passion for space exploration, artificial intelligence, engineering, and innovation.

Our mission is to transform bold ideas into meaningful solutions by combining scientific research, creative thinking, and emerging technologies. Through NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to tackle real-world challenges using open data, collaborative problem-solving, and technology.
summary: Mars Route is an Olympus Mons mission-planning and field-view prototype for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. It combines NASA elevation and imagery with route comparisons, historical dust observations and modeled environmental context. Users select a route, explore the terrain and follow a simulated rover-and-EVA science expedition while tracking scenario resources.
details:
The planning map displays elevation, slope, shaded relief and orbital imagery. A grid-based A* search compares shortest, balanced and slope-weighted paths subject to the selected slope limit and a threshold derived from a radiation model. Users can place a start and destination, compare route distance and ascent, and open the field view.

The OLY-01 scenario simulates an expedition to a caldera survey station, including rover and walking legs, optional resupply, three timed records and return to base. A 3D map and helmet-style display show simulated movement, resource estimates and environmental context. The application runs locally and its core map and simulation are available offline.

MOLA’s approximately 1.4 km grid cannot resolve individual obstacles. Dust data are historical, temperature values are climate-model outputs, and radiation values derive from a published model. Equipment values, bases and mission operations are scenario assumptions. The software does not establish astronaut safety or provide live telemetry.

The application uses JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Canvas, WebGL2 and a Python local server. Claude Code, DeepSeek and OpenAI Codex assisted with development, debugging and test preparation under team direction.
